title: Tech Note: Security via data encryption
author: Frank Chang

historical_commentary.text: Explaining and implementing RSA from first principles in 4D methods was a genuinely useful educational exercise in 2003, when 4D developers had few built-in cryptography options and needed to understand the underlying math to secure their own protocols. Data encryption itself remains as critical a concern today as ever, but this specific from-scratch, real-number-arithmetic RSA implementation is now clearly superseded: modern 4D provides built-in, standards-based encryption commands (e.g. Generate encryption keypair, Encrypt data/Decrypt data, and X.509-based key management) plus native TLS/SSL support for transport security, all of which are far more secure and performant than a hand-rolled demo intended for teaching rather than production use.
related_updates: Current 4D versions provide built-in cryptography commands (e.g. Generate encryption keypair, Encrypt data, Decrypt data) rather than requiring a from-scratch RSA implementation
Native TLS/SSL support in 4D's HTTP/network layers now handles transport-level encryption that this note's manual approach did not address
